programme: MYF6 and KLF15 sit on a skeletal-muscle transcriptional-differentiation/metabolic axis (MYF6 co-targets MYOG and MEF2A, the classic myogenic-regulatory-factor partnership; KLF15 targets SLC2A4, PPARGC1A and NR3C1, the muscle metabolic/glucocorticoid arm). ARID4A (via RB1 and SIN3A), HCFC1 and TFDP3 converge on the same E2F node (E2F1/E2F3/E2F4/E2F5, CDC6, CCNA2) that muscle cells must silence to exit the cell cycle before terminal differentiation, and NCOA1 is a nuclear-receptor/MRF coactivator that can potentiate either arm.
role_in_a: In fibromyalgia this axis has essentially no direct standing in the record: every factor is blank in Open Targets, and the only disease-relevant citation (NCOA1, 38590761) is about a steroid-receptor/LXR pain-modulation mechanism, not about MRF- or E2F-driven muscle transcription.
role_in_b: In sarcoma the pieces that are placed point at differentiation failure and cell-cycle deregulation in muscle-lineage tumors: MYF6 is studied as an MRF in rhabdomyosarcoma (35933111, though that specific paper reports a negative result), and NCOA1 recurs as a fusion partner (MEIS1::NCOA1) in spindle-cell sarcomas, consistent with aberrant coactivator function rather than the normal MRF program.
shared_axis: If real, the link would be that skeletal muscle is both the tissue of origin for MRF-driven sarcomas and a site of reported (though not evidenced here) peripheral pathology in fibromyalgia, so the same MRF/Rb-E2F/coactivator circuit that runs normal myogenic differentiation could be blocked in one disease (malignant dedifferentiation) and dysregulated in the other (muscle metabolic/pain symptoms) — but nothing in the retrieved material states this connection directly.
reasoning: The six carrying factors do name a real, textbook module (MRF-MEF2 differentiation coupled to Rb-E2F cell-cycle exit, with NCOA1 as coactivator), so this is not incoherent. But the sarcoma citations are scattered across unrelated sarcoma subtypes and mechanisms (a negative RMS splicing result, fusion-oncoprotein case reports), and fibromyalgia contributes almost nothing beyond one tangential pain-pathway paper, so the cross-disease link rests on inference, not retrieved evidence.
support: 35933111 — studies MYF6 exon skipping in rhabdomyosarcoma but reports it as not found, so it places MYF6 as a subject of RMS differentiation research without confirming this specific mechanism; 38590761 — places NCOA1 in an LXR/estrogen pain-modulation pathway relevant to fibromyalgia's female-predominant, estrogen-linked pathophysiology; 40420135 and 40160183 — describe MEIS1::NCOA1 fusion sarcomas (pelvic, renal spindle-cell), evidence of NCOA1 as an oncogenic fusion partner rather than normal-function coactivator; 42449878 — a further MEIS1::NCOA2/NCOA1-family fusion sarcoma case report, same caveat.
how_to_falsify: Profile MYF6/MEF2A target-gene expression (MYOG, CKM) and Rb-E2F target expression (CCNA2, CDC6) in fibromyalgia muscle biopsies versus matched controls: if this module shows no differential activity in fibromyalgia muscle, the fibromyalgia side of the account fails. On the sarcoma side, test whether MYF6 knockdown in a rhabdomyosarcoma line changes differentiation-gene output (MYOG, CKM) — a null result would be consistent with the existing negative splicing finding (35933111) and would further weaken the module's relevance to this sarcoma subtype specifically.
caveats: Fibromyalgia has zero Open Targets association for all 12 factors, and the 40 patient-group comparisons are drawn from only 3 independent cohort pairs, so replication depth is much shallower than the comparison count suggests. The sarcoma citations span biologically distinct entities (rhabdomyosarcoma, chordoma, myeloid/erythroid 'sarcoma', spindle-cell and myoepithelial fusion tumors) rather than one disease process, and several are gene-fusion case reports (oncogenic rewiring) rather than evidence of the factor's normal regulatory role; the KLF15 sarcoma citations specifically describe KLF17 fusions, a related but distinct KLF-family member, not KLF15 itself. ATF4 and CBFA2T3 were excluded from carrying_factors because their evidence points to different mechanisms (proteostatic stress in chordoma; corepressor fusions in myeloid/erythroid disease) that do not integrate with the MRF/Rb-E2F module. Tissue-generic exclusions (SREBF2, IRF5, IKZF1, RUNX2, MEF2C, STAT1, and others) removed several muscle- and immune-adjacent regulators before ranking, so their absence here is by design, not a gap in this account.
